summary.headline: Steel Strips Wheels Q1 FY27 revenue rose about 27% YoY to INR1,509 crore, with standalone EBITDA per wheel at INR314 versus INR262 a year earlier.
summary.overview: Management reported revenue of INR1,509 crore (about 27% YoY) and standalone EBITDA with other income of INR165.17 crore (up 32% YoY), with PAT up 43% YoY to INR71.51 crore and PAT margin at 4.7%. Management attributes the EBITDA-per-wheel gain mainly to OEM input-price increases (beyond raw materials), operating leverage, and mix shift toward premium products. Exports were still down YoY, but management said June exports rose 7% and Q1 exports recovered about 37% sequentially after US tariffs settled at 10%. Management raised its EBITDA-per-wheel expectation to more than INR310 for FY27 and reiterated 20%+ top-line growth, with a Bhuj aluminium expansion due for trial production in Q4 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: Passed on to customers with a lag

segments.name: Alloy wheels
segments.commentary: Contribute about 35% of revenue; management cites a leadership position in domestic market and rising passenger-vehicle penetration. Bhuj capacity to be expanded by 1.2 million wheels.

segments.name: Aluminium knuckles
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR23 crore; management guides FY27 knuckles revenue of INR110-130 crore, roughly double FY26. Plant running at 100% utilisation with order book sold out; Bhuj capacity 1.1 million units. Customers are Mahindra plus one newly acquired customer.

segments.name: Truck and tractor wheels
segments.commentary: Truck and tractor together cited at about 34% of revenue. Tractors described as high value-added with stable replacement demand; truck demand had a small blip last month, which management expects to improve after monsoon.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Management targets about INR600 crore for FY27 and expects 20%+ growth next year, constrained by capacity. Management said Vietnam and Thailand no longer hold a duty advantage over India.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth target of 20%+; analysts cite about INR6,500 crore, with management endorsing a 35-37% alloy share of that.
EBITDA per wheel to rise from about INR262 in FY26 to more than INR310 in FY27; management says upside bias on INR314 and to review after Q2.
Standalone EBITDA of about INR650 crore on INR6,500 crore revenue was referenced by analysts; management did not dispute it.
Bhuj aluminium wheel (1.2 million) and knuckles (1.1 million) plants: trial production expected in Q4 FY27; new capacity expected to run at 80%+ in Q1 FY28.

Total FY27 capex about INR600 crore including about INR420 crore Bhuj expansion, about INR80 crore replacement and other capex, and about INR150 crore Brownfield agricultural/passenger-car steel wheel line (partly in FY27, partly FY28).
Management expects steel passenger-car wheel demand to grow more than 5%.
capex_capacity: Bhuj aluminium wheel plant: 1.2 million wheels per year; knuckles plant: 1.1 million units per year (Pranav Jain cited 0.6 million knuckles capacity expansion in the capex discussion); trial production expected Q4 FY27.
Total aluminium capacity to reach about 6.2 million wheels after Bhuj expansion.

Brownfield steel wheel line of about INR150 crore for agricultural and fungible passenger-car wheels; adds up to about 2 million wheels across the Chandigarh plant; steel wheel capacity to go from about 24 million to about 26 million; commercialisation targeted before calendar year-end, with results in Q4.
Utilisation: all business units running above 95%; knuckles at 100%.
Management is evaluating further aluminium and knuckles expansion, and hot stamping for OEM relationships; nothing firm yet, decision in 3-6 months depending on export profile.
demand_pricing: Input price increases of 1% to 5% from OEMs; management says almost all increases received, with some still to flow. Management attributes about 1%+ margin uplift to these increases.
Aluminium pass-through is now monthly with about 30-day reimbursement lag, versus quarterly earlier; management says it is back-to-back neutral.

Competition in domestic aluminium wheels: two serious players; management says prices have fallen but SSWL earns a premium in some cases due to technical superiority. Competitors are bidding below cost.
Exports: management says demand is recovering and new OEM programmes outside the US are ramping up over the remaining three quarters of FY27.
Domestic truck segment saw a small blip last month; tractor demand is robust with price reductions widening the farmer base.

qa_highlights.question: Given Q1 EBITDA per wheel of INR309 against FY27 guidance of INR300, will it fall over the next three quarters or will guidance be raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR314 is a benchmark with upside bias; it will review after Q2 and avoided guiding to INR325 or INR350. Product mix, West Asia and commodity prices are the swing factors.

qa_highlights.question: Why did exports fall YoY from INR160 crore last quarter to INR127 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the YoY fall to a period of tariff uncertainty versus Vietnam and Thailand; June exports rose 7% and Q1 exports recovered about 37% QoQ. Management expects no tariff headwind in the remaining three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and its breakdown?
qa_highlights.answer: Pranav Jain: about INR420 crore for Bhuj alloy wheel (1.2 million) and knuckles (0.6 million) capacity, plus about INR80 crore replacement and other capex, totalling about INR500 crore. Management added about INR150 crore for a Brownfield agricultural wheel line, so total is about INR600 crore plus or minus.

qa_highlights.question: What is the borrowing cost and why does interest expense look higher than borrowings imply?
qa_highlights.answer: Total borrowings were about INR826 crore in FY26 at 8% to 9% interest. Management said the higher P&L finance cost reflects factoring limits of INR400-500 crore used when funds are needed; aluminium cost increases of over INR150 crore also tied up working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Is SSWL the lowest-cost steel and alloy producer globally?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said this is about 80-90% true, and that outside China it is the lowest-cost producer; China's costs are hard to compare due to subsidies.

qa_highlights.question: Are alloy wheel margins at risk from commoditisation and rising imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said only two serious domestic players dominate aluminium wheels and SSWL earns a premium on technical superiority in some cases. Margin confidence rests on export diversification rather than the domestic market.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Chinese partner Arays' role in the Bhuj plant?
qa_highlights.answer: Aditya Dixit said Arays will provide technical support, mainly for aftermarket wheels; the Bhuj plant is primarily for export aftermarket, with some capacity for OEMs. He declined to give more detail.

qa_highlights.question: When will the new capacities reach optimum utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects at least 80% utilisation of both Bhuj units in Q1 FY28, with knuckles possibly earlier. Management declined to commit to a further capex cycle until new capacity sells.

risks_watch: Raw material (aluminium and steel) price volatility and West Asia conflict; management says pass-through is now monthly with a 30-day lag.
Truck segment softness in the domestic market, which management expects to recover after monsoon.
Export recovery needs to be sustained; June was up 7% but FY27 export target of about INR600 crore needs sustained growth.
Knuckles ramp-up: Q1 revenue about INR23 crore, and FY27 guidance of INR110-130 crore needs a strong H2.
Finance cost above the implied 8-9% on borrowings, driven by factoring; watch working capital.
Bhuj capacity commissioning timeline (Q4 FY27 trial) and steel Brownfield line (before calendar year-end).
Management did not give steel vs alloy EBITDA-per-wheel split; will address next call.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on demand, pricing and capacity, with some reluctance to guide beyond current numbers. Management was cautious on margin trajectory ("don't jump the gun") and openly declined to disclose the steel versus alloy split. Some answers were loose on specifics (e.g., EBITDA per wheel figures, PAT target).

growth.why: Management reiterates FY27 top-line growth of 20%+ (about INR6,500 crore cited by analysts) with Bhuj aluminium wheel (1.2m) and knuckles (1.1m) capacity and a Chandigarh steel line due in Q4 FY27 and running at 80%+ in Q1 FY28, but no firm order book for the incremental volume beyond knuckles (INR110-130 crore guided, sold out) and exports constrained by capacity.
